title: Consolidate runtime rpath handling and ABI gating for heterogeneous quantized kernels
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: multiple service incidents and noisy startup traces indicate inconsistent rpath/RUNPATH handling across our GPU runtime images. This causes spurious fallback to legacy kernel bundles, duplicate symbol loads, and a measurable cold-start latency penalty for quantized kernels that link different CUTLASS/Triton variants. Goal: unify runtime rpath handling and add an explicit ABI-gating layer so each model-serving process deterministically picks the correct kernel bundle variant, with a safe opt-out fallback and audit logging. This reduces probe jitter, prevents mixed-symbol loads, and makes kernel ABI mismatches detectable before user requests are served.
acceptance_criteria: Single canonical rpath resolution path implemented in runtime loader and documented
Introduce REDWOOD_ABI_GUARD env var to opt into strict ABI enforcement; default enabled for dedicated and private tiers
All CI images pass new "abi-sanity" integration test that exercises mixed-cutlass/cuda combinations
Canary rollout on 5% of dedicated pool shows no increased 95th pct latency and <1% increased error rate
Rollback path implemented that reverts to legacy rpath behavior via feature flag without image rebuild
Security review completed and KMS/HSM secrets not exposed by loader changes
technical_notes: Problem vector: we observed that RUNPATH entries added by prelink/build-time packaging were inconsistently applied when process was sandboxed with LD_LIBRARY_PATH and preload hooks. This led to duplicate symbols between cutlass_v1 and cutlass_v2 bundles.

Design: implement rpath-normalizer in runtime bootstrap that canonicalizes candidate library paths into a deterministic order (vendor-sorted + manifest-priority) and then sets a process-specific secure RUNPATH via dlmopen or by rewriting the ELF PT_DYNAMIC at startup for supported kernels.

ABI gating: introduce a lightweight ABI manifest file next to kernel bundles that contains architecture fingerprint, cutlass-version, triton-plugin-version and export a small verifier used during warmup. The verifier runs in a chrooted validator process and records to audit logs.

Fallback policy: if verifier fails, runtime will attempt up to N=2 automatic bundle substitutions (compatible lower-precision or older-cutlass bundle) before marking node unhealthy and routing to fallback pool.
Build changes: add -Wl,--enable-new-dtags and normalized LD_RUN_PATH generation in packaging pipeline; add rpath-normalizer unit tests to buildkite matrix
Performance: measure cold-start change — expected median cold-start down ~8-12ms due to reduced symbol resolution retries; worst-case improvement when previously falling back to older bundles.
Security: loader and verifier run with minimal capabilities; no KMS access required; ensure verifier logs do not contain plaintext paths that reveal customer model names.
testing_plan: Unit: add rpath-normalizer unit tests verifying ordering, dedupe and edge cases (missing libs, relative paths)

Integration: abi-sanity test that spins an isolated validator process, mounts kernel bundles, and asserts no symbol collisions for combinations: (cutlass_v1+cudnn8), (cutlass_v2+cudnn9), (cutlass_v2+triton3)
Regression: run existing GPU probe suite across heterogeneous node pool with variable CUDA driver versions (11.8, 12.1, 12.3)
Performance: perf-runner scenarios for cold-start and steady-state 99th pct token latency; compare baseline runtime-1.18 image
Chaos: briefly toggle REDWOOD_ABI_GUARD=false on a canary subset and assert safe fallback path triggers without user-visible errors
rollout_plan: Stage 1: merge PRs and publish runtime-1.19-canary images to internal registry
Stage 2: deploy to canary dedicated pool (5% traffic) with extended tracing and audit logs enabled for 48h
Stage 3: evaluate metrics (errors, 95/99 latency, kernel fallback counts) and security artifacts; hold if any regression >3% on 95th pct latency or >0.5% change in error rate
Stage 4: progressive ramp to 25% then 100% over 2 weeks if metrics stable; enable for hosted tier after Dedicated success
Rollback: flip runtime feature flag runtime.loader.legacy_rpath=true at orchestration layer to restore previous behavior instantly; follow with image rollback if necessary
qa_checklist: Smoke: start 10 containers across mixed GPU nodes and verify startup logs contain 'rpath-normalizer: OK'
Audit: verify abi verifier produced signed snapshot in S3 path s3://redwood-audit/abi-snapshots/YYYYMMDD/ENG-214577
Canary tests: synthetic prompt suite for 20 small and 10 long-context models; ensure outputs match baseline within tolerated drift thresholds
Security: confirm loader changes passed internal static analysis and no new SUID/privilege increases

notes_for_reviewers: Focus on the ABI manifest format and whether we should include a cryptographic signature for bundle provenance (tradeoff: adds packaging complexity)
Evaluate the implications of rewriting PT_DYNAMIC at startup — some older kernels may not support safe rewrites; we already have fallback path. Documentation must be explicit.
Packaging: confirm no increase in image size >2% due to validator binary; if larger, consider splitting validator into a separate build artifact used only at warmup time
